hub.title: Free Public Data Tables: Population, GDP, Country Codes and More | cv.cm
hub.description: Open data tables you can search, sort and download as CSV: population, GDP and GDP (PPP), GNI, exports, inflation, unemployment, poverty and income inequality (Gini), military spending, foreign reserves, life expectancy, doctors, literacy, murder and suicide rates, alcohol and tobacco use, birth and death rates, migrants, land and forest area, CO2 emissions, air pollution, electricity, internet, mobile and broadband use, ISO country and currency codes, calling codes, time zones, paper sizes and ASCII.
hub.lede: Plain tables of public data from the World Bank, ISO and IANA. Search, sort by any column, or download the CSV. Every table names its source and licence.
about: Each table is a snapshot of an official source, refreshed from that source and dated on the page. Country figures come from the World Bank World Development Indicators (CC BY 4.0). Codes come from the ISO 3166 and ISO 4217 lists and the IANA time zone database.
Numbers are shown in your language, but the CSV files keep raw values and ISO codes, so they open cleanly in Excel, Google Sheets or code.

faq.q: Where does this data come from?
faq.a: Country statistics are from the World Bank World Development Indicators. Country, currency and dialing codes follow ISO 3166, ISO 4217 and the ITU list. Time zones are from the IANA tz database. Paper sizes follow ISO 216, ISO 269, JIS P 0138 and ANSI.

faq.q: Can I use these tables for free?
faq.a: Yes. World Bank data is licensed CC BY 4.0, so credit the World Bank when you reuse it. Codes and reference tables are public facts you can reuse freely.

faq.q: How current are the numbers?
faq.a: Each page shows the date of its snapshot and the year of every value. The World Bank publishes most indicators a year or two after the fact, so a country's latest value can be from an earlier year.

Cold and very hot climates use more for heating and air conditioning. A household fridge uses roughly 300 to 500 kWh a year.

Many people in Africa and South Asia go online mainly through mobile networks, so low fixed broadband there does not mean few internet users.

gdp-ppp.name: GDP (PPP) by country
gdp-ppp.title: GDP (PPP) by Country {to}: Largest Economies by Purchasing Power | cv.cm
gdp-ppp.description: GDP at purchasing power parity for {rows} economies in current international dollars, ranked, with share of the world. World {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.

facts: Largest economies by purchasing power: {top1} ({v1}), {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).
about: An international dollar buys the same basket of goods and services in every country as a US dollar buys in the United States. Converting GDP this way removes price differences, so countries where living costs are low rank higher than they do at market exchange rates.
PPP is the better measure of how much an economy actually produces and consumes; GDP at exchange rates is the better measure of what it can buy abroad.

faq.q: Which country has the largest GDP by PPP?
faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.q: What is the difference between GDP (PPP) and nominal GDP?
faq.a: Nominal GDP converts each economy at market exchange rates. GDP (PPP) uses rates that equalise the price of the same goods everywhere, so it compares the volume of output, not its value in dollars.

faq.q: What is world GDP at PPP?
faq.a: {world} in {worldYear}, in current international dollars.

about: Some countries measure income and others measure consumption, which is spread more evenly than income. Most of Asia and Africa survey consumption, so their Gini values look lower than they would on income; compare countries that use the same measure.
Surveys are run every few years, so each row shows the latest one within ten years. The World Bank does not publish a world Gini index.

faq.q: Which country has the highest income inequality?
faq.a: {top1}, with a Gini index of {v1} in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.q: What is a good Gini coefficient?
faq.a: There is no target value. Most European countries are between about 25 and 35; values above 40 are usually called high inequality, and above 50 very high.

Surveys are run every few years, so each row shows the latest one within ten years. Many high-income countries are not surveyed against this line and are not in the list. A 0.0 means the survey found almost no one below the line.

faq.q: What are the poorest countries in the world?
faq.a: By share of people below $3.00 a day: {top1} ({v1}% in {year1}), {top2} ({v2}%) and {top3} ({v3}%).

faq.a: $3.00 a day per person at 2021 purchasing power parity, set by the World Bank in 2025.

about: Most high-income countries stopped measuring basic literacy decades ago, because nearly everyone has gone to school; the United States, Japan, Germany, the United Kingdom, France and Korea are not in the list for that reason, not because their rates are low.
Figures come from censuses and surveys every several years, so each row shows the latest within ten years. Literacy is usually self-reported, so small differences near 100% say little.

homicide-rate.title: Murder Rate by Country {to}: Homicides per 100,000, Safest and Most Dangerous | cv.cm

homicide-rate.lede: Intentional homicides for every 100,000 people in {rows} countries and areas, ranked from the most to the least violent. Source: World Bank, from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
about: An intentional homicide is a death deliberately caused by another person, including killings in gang violence and domestic violence. Deaths in wars and other armed conflicts are not counted, so some countries at war look safer than they are.

The murder rate is the most comparable crime figure between countries, because a body is hard to miss; most other crimes depend on what people report to the police. Small islands can rank high on a handful of cases.

faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} homicides per 100,000 people in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.a: {world} intentional homicides per 100,000 people in {worldYear}.

suicide-rate.title: Suicide Rate by Country {to}: Deaths per 100,000 in {rows} Countries | cv.cm
suicide-rate.description: Suicide deaths per 100,000 people in {rows} countries, ranked from highest to lowest. World {world} ({worldYear}). WHO data via the World Bank, CSV download.

suicide-rate.lede: Suicide deaths in a year for every 100,000 people in {rows} countries, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from the World Health Organization Global Health Estimates.
about: These are WHO estimates, not raw death registrations: many countries do not record every cause of death, and suicide is often under-reported where it carries stigma or legal penalties. Low figures in some countries partly reflect that.
If you or someone you know is struggling, please contact a local crisis line or emergency service. Help is available, and talking to someone can make a difference.

faq.q: Which country has the highest suicide rate?
faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} suicide deaths per 100,000 people in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.q: What is the world suicide rate?
faq.a: {world} deaths per 100,000 people in {worldYear}.

faq.q: Why might a country's suicide rate be undercounted?
faq.a: Where suicide carries stigma or is a crime, deaths are often recorded under other causes. The WHO adjusts for this, but the lowest figures are the least certain.

about: One litre of pure alcohol is about 60 cans of beer (330 ml at 5%) or 10 bottles of wine (750 ml at 13%). The figure includes home-made and smuggled alcohol, which the WHO estimates, and drinking by tourists, which raises small tourist destinations.

These are WHO projections; the latest year is the one the World Bank publishes. Countries that ban alcohol and report exactly zero are left out, because the zero is a missing estimate, not a measurement.

faq.a: {top1}, with {v1} litres of pure alcohol per person aged 15+ in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.a: {world} litres of pure alcohol per person aged 15+ worldwide in {worldYear}. One litre is about 60 cans of beer, so that is a few hundred cans a year if it were all beer.

faq.q: Which country drinks the least alcohol?
faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast} litres per person.

tobacco-use.lede: Share of people aged 15 and over who currently smoke or use any other tobacco product, daily or not, in {rows} countries, ranked from highest to lowest. Source: World Bank, from WHO age-standardised estimates.
about: Tobacco use covers cigarettes, cigars, pipes, water pipes, and smokeless tobacco such as chewing tobacco and snus. E-cigarettes without tobacco are not counted.
The WHO age-standardises the rates, so a country with a young population is compared fairly with an older one. Men use tobacco far more than women in most countries.

faq.a: {top1}, where {v1}% of adults used tobacco in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}%) and {top3} ({v3}%).

air-pollution.name: Air pollution (PM2.5) by country
air-pollution.title: Most Polluted Countries {to}: PM2.5 Air Pollution by Country | cv.cm
air-pollution.description: Average yearly exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5), µg/m³, for {rows} countries, ranked from most to least polluted. World {world} ({worldYear}). World Bank data, CSV download.
air-pollution.lede: Average yearly concentration of fine particles (PM2.5) in the air people breathe, weighted by where people live, for {rows} countries and areas, ranked from most to least polluted. Source: World Bank, from the Global Burden of Disease study.
about: PM2.5 are particles 2.5 micrometres or smaller, small enough to reach deep into the lungs. The WHO guideline is an annual average of 5 µg/m³; almost every country is above it.

These are modelled from satellites and ground monitors and weighted by population, so they describe what the average resident breathes, not the worst city. Desert dust counts too, which is why Gulf and Sahel countries rank high.

faq.q: Which country has the worst air pollution?
faq.a: {top1}, with an average PM2.5 exposure of {v1} µg/m³ in {year1}, followed by {top2} ({v2}) and {top3} ({v3}).

faq.a: In this list, {last}, at {vlast} µg/m³.

country-codes.name: Country codes (ISO 3166)
country-codes.title: ISO 3166 Country Codes: Alpha-2, Alpha-3 and Numeric List of {rows} Countries | cv.cm
country-codes.description: All {rows} ISO 3166-1 country codes: two-letter (alpha-2), three-letter (alpha-3) and numeric codes, plus internet domain and continent. Searchable, CSV download.
country-codes.lede: Two-letter, three-letter and numeric codes for all {rows} countries and territories in ISO 3166-1, with each one's internet domain and continent.
facts: {rows} countries and territories have an ISO 3166-1 code.
Alpha-2 codes are used for internet domains (.jp, .de) and in language tags (en-US).
Alpha-3 codes appear on passports; numeric codes come from the UN M49 standard.
about: ISO 3166-1 gives every country and many dependent territories three codes. Alpha-2 (US, CN) is the one most systems use. Alpha-3 (USA, CHN) is easier to read. The numeric code (840, 156) works where Latin letters do not.
The UK uses .uk for its internet domain although its ISO code is GB. Names here are in your language.

faq.q: What is the difference between alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes?
faq.a: Alpha-2 codes have two letters (JP) and are used in domains, language tags and most software. Alpha-3 codes have three letters (JPN) and are used on passports and in statistics.

faq.q: How many ISO country codes are there?
faq.a: ISO 3166-1 lists {rows} countries and territories, each with an alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric code.

faq.q: What is the country code for the United Kingdom?
faq.a: GB (alpha-2), GBR (alpha-3) and 826 (numeric). Its internet domain is .uk.

calling-codes.name: International calling codes
calling-codes.title: International Calling Codes: Country Dialing Code List ({rows} Countries) | cv.cm
calling-codes.description: Country calling codes for {rows} countries and territories, from +1 to +998. Search by country or code, with ISO codes. CSV download.
calling-codes.lede: The number to dial after the international prefix (+) to reach each of {rows} countries and territories.
facts: Dial + (or your country's exit code, such as 00 or 011), then the country code, then the number without its leading 0.
+1 is shared by the US, Canada and many Caribbean islands, which add a 3-digit area code.
+7 is shared by Russia and Kazakhstan.
about: Calling codes are assigned by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU-T E.164). Codes are one to three digits long, and some groups of countries share one code.
On a mobile phone, hold 0 to type +. It works from any country, so you do not need to know the local exit code.

faq.q: How do I call another country?
faq.a: Type + (or your exit code, such as 00 in most countries or 011 in the US), the country code, then the local number without its leading 0.

faq.q: Which country is +86?
faq.a: +86 is China. +852 is Hong Kong, +853 Macao and +886 Taiwan.

faq.q: Why do several countries share +1?
faq.a: They are in the North American Numbering Plan. The 3-digit area code after +1 tells you the country.

currency-codes.name: Currency codes (ISO 4217)
currency-codes.title: ISO 4217 Currency Codes: List of {rows} Currencies with Symbols | cv.cm
currency-codes.description: All {rows} active ISO 4217 currency codes with numeric code, symbol, decimal places and the countries that use each one. Searchable, CSV download.
currency-codes.lede: Three-letter codes, numeric codes, symbols and decimal places for the {rows} currencies in ISO 4217, and where each one is used.
facts: ISO 4217 lists {rows} active currency codes, including funds and precious metals.
The first two letters are usually the ISO country code: JPY is Japan's yen.
Codes starting with X are not tied to a country: XAU is gold, XDR is the IMF's special drawing right.
about: Banks, payment systems and accounting software use ISO 4217 codes because symbols are ambiguous: $ is used by more than 20 currencies.
Decimals is the number of minor-unit digits (cents). JPY and KRW have none, and some Gulf currencies have three.

faq.q: What is the currency code for the Chinese yuan?
faq.a: CNY, numeric code 156. Offshore yuan is often quoted as CNH, but that is a market convention, not an ISO code.

faq.q: How many currencies are there?
faq.a: ISO 4217 lists {rows} active codes, including a few funds, precious metals and testing codes.

faq.q: Why does the euro have one code for many countries?
faq.a: EUR is one currency shared by the euro area, so it has one code. The Used in column lists every country and territory that uses it.

time-zones.name: Time zones (IANA)
time-zones.title: List of Time Zones with UTC Offsets ({rows} IANA Time Zones, {year}) | cv.cm
time-zones.description: All {rows} IANA time zones (Asia/Shanghai, America/New_York) with their UTC offsets in January and July {year}, so you can see daylight saving time. CSV download.
time-zones.lede: Every IANA time zone with its UTC offset in January and July {year}. Where the two differ, the zone uses daylight saving time.
facts: {rows} IANA time zone IDs, sorted from west ({west}) to east ({east}).
A zone whose January and July offsets differ observes daylight saving time.
Some zones are offset by 30 or 45 minutes, such as India (UTC+05:30) and Nepal (UTC+05:45).
about: IANA time zone IDs such as Europe/London are what phones, computers and programming languages use. This list follows IANA's zone.tab: one row per country and zone, each carrying that area's daylight saving rules.
Offsets are calculated for 15 January and 15 July {year} from the {tz} tz database. Governments sometimes change their rules at short notice.

faq.q: What time zone is China in?
faq.a: All of China uses China Standard Time, UTC+08:00, all year. The IANA ID is Asia/Shanghai.

faq.q: What is the difference between UTC and GMT?
faq.a: For everyday use they are the same time. UTC is the atomic time standard; GMT is the time zone at 0° longitude, which the UK uses in winter.

faq.q: How many time zones are there?
faq.a: The IANA database used here has {rows} zone IDs. They use fewer than 40 distinct UTC offsets.

paper-sizes.name: Paper sizes
paper-sizes.title: Paper Sizes Chart: A4, A3, B5, Letter in mm, Inches and Pixels | cv.cm
paper-sizes.description: Dimensions of {rows} paper sizes (A0–A10, B, C, JIS B, Letter, Legal) in millimetres, inches and pixels at 300 and 96 DPI. CSV download.
paper-sizes.h1: Paper sizes in mm, inches and pixels
paper-sizes.lede: Width × height of ISO A, B and C sizes, Japanese JIS B sizes and North American sizes, with pixel sizes for printing (300 DPI) and screens (96 DPI).
facts: Each A size is half the one before it: two A4 sheets make one A3.
about: ISO 216 sizes keep the same 1:√2 shape, so a page scales from A4 to A3 or A5 without cropping. A0 has an area of one square metre.
JIS B sizes, common in Japan and China for notebooks and books, are slightly larger than ISO B. JIS B5 is 182 × 257 mm, while ISO B5 is 176 × 250 mm.

faq.q: What is the size of A4 paper?
faq.a: 210 × 297 mm, or 8.27 × 11.69 inches. At 300 DPI that is 2480 × 3508 pixels.

faq.q: What is the difference between A4 and Letter?
faq.a: A4 (210 × 297 mm) is narrower and taller than US Letter (215.9 × 279.4 mm). Most of the world uses A4; the US, Canada and Mexico use Letter.

faq.q: How many pixels do I need to print A4?
faq.a: 2480 × 3508 px for sharp prints at 300 DPI. 1240 × 1754 px (150 DPI) is enough for drafts.

ascii.name: ASCII table
ascii.title: ASCII Table: All 128 Codes in Decimal, Hex, Octal and Binary | cv.cm
ascii.description: Complete ASCII table of all 128 characters with decimal, hexadecimal, octal and binary values and control character names. CSV download.
ascii.lede: All 128 ASCII codes with their decimal, hex, octal and binary values, the character, and the name of each control character.
facts: Codes 0–31 and 127 are control characters; 32–126 are printable.
A is 65 (0x41) and a is 97 (0x61): upper and lower case differ by 32.
about: ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange, 1963) assigns 128 codes to English letters, digits, punctuation and control signals, using 7 bits.
UTF-8 encodes these 128 characters exactly as ASCII does, so every ASCII file is also valid UTF-8.

faq.q: What is the ASCII code for A?
faq.a: Capital A is 65 in decimal, 0x41 in hex and 1000001 in binary. Lowercase a is 97 (0x61).

faq.q: What is the ASCII code for a space?
faq.a: 32 in decimal, 0x20 in hex.

faq.q: What is the difference between LF and CR?
faq.a: LF (10, line feed) starts a new line on Linux and macOS. Windows text files end lines with CR LF (13 then 10).

hub.title: Rankings: AI Models, Market Share and More, with Sources | cv.cm
hub.description: Sourced rankings you can sort and download: best AI models, most used AI, browser, operating system, search engine, phone and social media market share, and the tallest mountains, longest rivers, largest lakes and islands.
hub.lede: Rankings built from open data, each with its source, licence and date. Sort any column, filter rows or download the CSV.
about: Every table here comes from a published source that allows reuse, and cv.cm does not add its own scores or place its own products in them. Read the About section on each page: most lists measure one thing, such as votes on one site or visits to tracked websites, and that limit matters.
Data is a dated snapshot rather than a live feed, so each page tells you which date it shows.

faq.q: Where does the data come from?
faq.a: AI quality comes from the Arena leaderboard, AI usage from OpenRouter, market share from StatCounter Global Stats, mountain heights from Wikidata, and rivers, lakes and islands from Wikipedia's lists. Each page links to its source and licence.

faq.q: How often are the rankings updated?
faq.a: They are refreshed automatically once a day and each page shows its data date. Sources publish at different speeds: market share is monthly, mountains, rivers, lakes and islands are checked monthly, AI tables change more often.

faq.q: Can I reuse these tables?
faq.a: Yes, under the source's licence shown on each page: CC BY 4.0 for the AI tables, CC BY-SA 3.0 for market share, CC0 (no conditions) for mountains and CC BY-SA 4.0 for rivers, lakes and islands. Credit the source. Most tables have a CSV download.
